newsitem.title: USA: Experian to halt free credit reports - LA Times.
newsitem.headline: Experian to halt free credit reports - LA Times.

text.p: Information services firm Experian will stop providing free credit reports to consumers beginning on March 1, the Los Angeles Times reported on Tuesday.
The company began the service in 1992 to give consumers free copies of their credit reports, the paper said.
The paper said the company's decision was due to lack of competition and abuses by credit repair clinics that inundated its offices with requests.
The paper said Experian will continue to provide free reports to consumers rejected for credit as required by law.
California-based Experian was bought by Britain's Great Universal Stores Plc in November for $1.7 billion.
